name: FORM Thursday + iRUN · Miami Season
protocol: Priorities: mile speed first, 5K speed endurance second, 10K durability third. All five athletes share identical Thursday work/splits, with Week14 Kevin taper exception. Six threshold Thursdays unchanged. Six future speed Thursdays add small controlled acceleration exposures and specific repeat targets; Week5 and Week11 5×400m are a comparable benchmark with the same 2:00 recovery. Monday iRUN is coach-reviewed against each Thursday and Forge; no automatic stacking.
pacing: Easy 8:00/mi or slower for Brice, Sam, David, Kevin; 4:58/km or slower for Tinius. Threshold effort RPE 6–7 where no numeric target exists. Thursday speed targets are shared coach-authored starting bands anchored to October 29 600m/200m prescription, not inferred personal PBs. Track reps display in m for everyone; Tinius and Simon use km outside track reps.
kevinSafety: Six miles published on October 31 is not evidence of prior long-run capacity. The proposed progression peaks at 16 miles on January 16 (15 days before race day), then tapers to 8 miles January 23 and 2 miles January 30. This pattern remains provisional until Kevin's running history, injury status, fueling practice and adaptation are reviewed. A 16-mile long run by itself does not establish readiness for a first 26.2-mile marathon; the race-day assignment stays a coach-held draft until evidence and actual registration support release.
week2: Preserve the October 29 5×600m (2:05–2:08) + 4×200m (40–41s) prescription and existing completions; athlete-facing label should be 5×600m + 4×200m without THE FIFTH CIRCLE, pending copy-only view fix.

speedCohortDescription: Speed Reserve is a running development program for runners who want to become faster over the mile and 5K without giving up their endurance. We use short track repetitions to improve speed and coordination, longer repetitions and controlled sustained running to help that speed last, and easy long runs to maintain endurance. The group shares Thursday track workouts, while each runner has their own goals and long-run distances.
